provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — .docm macro attachments are inspectable at the mail gateway and on the endpoint (Office child-process spawning, macro-security events); the specific lure/hashes are watchlistable, though initial delivery itself is partly off-victim
medium — WINWORD.EXE spawning wscript/powershell child processes and VBA macro execution are observable via process-lineage and Office/AMSI telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
detection_candidates.rationale: high — wscript/cscript executing a .vbs that decodes and launches PowerShell is observable via process-creation and script-block/command-line telemetry; the IEWebCache.vbs filename is a watchlist item

high — PowerShell script-block/module logging and AMSI capture the backdoor's script bodies, Base64-decoded content, and web/BITS activity; suspicious PowerShell launched from wscript/Office is high-fidelity
medium — PowerShell-initiated WMI queries are observable via WMI-activity and PowerShell logging, but system-profiling WMI use is common and needs process-lineage context

high — scheduled-task creation is logged (Event ID 4698 / Task Scheduler operational); the task name 'IE Web Cache' and a task launching wscript/rundll32 on a masquerading DLL are actor-specific, high-fidelity detections

high — creation/modification of unusual values under the Shell Extensions key holding high-entropy (RC4/encrypted) blobs is detectable via registry-audit and EDR registry telemetry; the specific value names are a strong watchlist
medium — registry reads of the specific config value names correlate with the backdoor process, but registry queries in general are high-volume and need process context

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — high-entropy registry blobs and Base64-encoded script bodies are detectable via entropy/encoding heuristics on registry and script-block telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Command Obfuscation
detection_candidates.rationale: high — Base64-encoded PowerShell (-enc / FromBase64String) invoked from a VBS loader is detectable via script-block logging and command-line encoding heuristics
medium — decode/decrypt routines are inferred from script-block content rather than a discrete event; detectable when script-block logging captures the decode calls

detection_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — benign-looking task/file names and lookalike infrastructure domains are detectable via name/path baselining and DNS analytics, but require known-bad lists or anomaly baselining
medium — host-profiling commands via PowerShell/WMI are observable but common; value from process-lineage correlation to the macro/VBS chain
medium — network-config discovery commands are observable in command-line/PowerShell logs but are common admin actions requiring correlation
medium — whoami/user-context queries are observable but noisy; meaningful mainly in a recon-burst process window
medium — process enumeration is observable via command-line/API telemetry but common; correlate with backdoor process lineage

detection_candidates.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — access to browser credential-store files/APIs is detectable via file-access and process-access telemetry on the browser profile paths

detection_candidates.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Windows Credential Manager
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — access to Credential Manager vault files and vaultcmd/credential APIs is detectable via file/process-access telemetry
medium — automated bulk local collection is detectable via file-access-burst and staging patterns tied to the backdoor process, but blends with legitimate activity
medium — local data collection is common; suspicious mainly via staging and process-lineage context tied to the implant

high — anomalous BITS jobs to external/non-Microsoft hosts are a strong, actor-signature detection: BITS-Client operational log (Event IDs 3/59/60), bitsadmin/PowerShell BITS cmdlet usage, and non-browser/non-updater processes creating BITS transfers to unknown domains
medium — HTTP callbacks to the known C2 domains are detectable via proxy/DNS telemetry and domain blocklists, but generic web C2 blends with normal traffic absent the IOC list

medium — the encryption itself is not directly observable, but RC4-encrypted payloads over HTTP/BITS to unknown domains and hardcoded-key artifacts support signature/hunt detection when combined with the IOCs
medium — download of follow-on payloads via BITS/HTTP is detectable via BITS job creation with a local file target and file-write-after-network telemetry
medium — outbound BITS upload jobs to external hosts and data egress correlated with the C2 domains are detectable via BITS-Client log and proxy/DLP telemetry
medium — periodic/beaconing BITS upload jobs on a fixed interval to a fixed domain set are detectable via BITS-job and network-beaconing analytics

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — actor-controlled social-media personas and rapport-building occur off-victim; intel/brand-monitoring and takedown candidate, not endpoint-observable
low — sender-account creation is off-victim; hunt/intel candidate via sender-reputation and lookalike-domain monitoring
low — adversary domain acquisition is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via infrastructure tracking, passive DNS and newly-registered-lookalike-domain monitoring
low — off-victim link-staging/tracking infrastructure; intel/hunt candidate via link-pattern (/aax.me/[0-9a-f]{5}/) blocklisting and web-proxy monitoring
low — capability development is off-victim; intel/attribution signal, not endpoint-observable

low — link-based delivery through a third-party shortener is largely off-victim social engineering; hunt candidate via email/URL gateway logs for the aax.me pattern rather than crisp endpoint detection
low — user click on an external link is a social action; hunt candidate via proxy/URL telemetry for the aax.me link pattern
low — the profiling JavaScript executes in the target's browser against off-victim infrastructure; not endpoint-observable in enterprise logs, intel/hunt candidate only
low — AV port-probing executes browser-side against off-victim infrastructure; not observable in standard endpoint telemetry, intel/hunt candidate
low — software/plugin enumeration occurs in the browser against attacker infrastructure; intel/hunt candidate rather than endpoint detection
